summary: The first divergence is the incomplete uhitm.c passive() AD_ELEC branch. On step 35, hitum() misses the living Energy Vortex but still calls passive(); C rolls d(6,4)=18, then rn2(3)=1, and prints the electrical jolt. JS passive() throws for this nonphysical passive attack before the matching rn2(3) and screen boundary. A whole-function file-port of passive() is actionable; the later step-43 gulpmu(AD_DREN) continuation is a separate mismatch, not this cause.

source.branch: passive() selects the first AT_NONE attack and computes its damage, then enters the second switch only when malive is true, mon->mcan is false, and rn2(3) is nonzero. Its AD_ELEC arm checks Shock_resistance and either reports a mild tingle with shield/resistance and golem effects or, without resistance, reports an electrical jolt and calls mdamageu(). This switch does not require mhitb, so it can affect the hero after a missed swing.
callers: uhitm.c hitum_cleave() at line 715 and hitum() at lines 789, 810; js/uhitm.js hitum() wires ordinary swings, while its Cleaver path currently refuses before passive().
uhitm.c hmonas() at lines 5827, 5829; js/uhitm.js hmonas() calls passive() after polymorphed attacks.
dokick.c kickdmg() at line 116 and kick_monster() at lines 158, 213, 219, 241, 265, 282; js/dokick.js kickdmg() and kick_monster() call passive().
dependencies: uhitm.c passive_obj() is a separate partial helper used by passive() for AD_FIRE, AD_ACID, AD_RUST, AD_CORR, and AD_ENCH object effects. It does not run on this AD_ELEC branch; keep its independent object-effect scope explicit if implementation work extends beyond the first divergence.

evidence: nethack-c/upstream/include/monsters.h:1081-1090 defines Energy Vortex with a third mattk entry AT_NONE/AD_ELEC/0d4 after its two active engulf attacks. nethack-c/upstream/src/uhitm.c:5865-5888 selects that first empty slot and draws the passive damage before testing the effect gate.

nethack-c/upstream/src/uhitm.c:6017-6020 gates the surviving-monster effects on malive, !mon->mcan, and rn2(3); :6103-6113 handles AD_ELEC. The AD_ELEC arm has no mhitb condition. nethack-c/upstream/src/uhitm.c:758-815 calls passive() from hitum() after known_hitum() even when its hit result is false.

challenges/cases/v19/energy-vortex-engulfs-and-drains-energy-c62-more.session.json (recording SHA-256 5e05a3bbfe84e3b21eb98d75c8630b84f806486bd6c1d6f408ddbd7a9b83cc62), segment 0 step 35, records key y, rnd(20)=15 at hitum, d(6,4)=18 at passive, then rn2(3)=1 at passive. Its screen says “You miss the energy vortex. You are jolted with electricity!” and status HP is 0; this confirms the miss still enters the AD_ELEC branch and its non-resisted damage arm.

js/uhitm.js:5299-5340 is a partial passive() port: it handles AD_ENCH and AD_PHYS, then throws “passive counter-attack” for the Energy Vortex AD_ELEC before the malive/!mcan/rn2(3) guard. The function is already called by the ordinary hitum() path at js/uhitm.js:2330, so the missing behavior is in the source-owned function rather than a missing caller.
